reviewer: Main agent; informed by study aims but condition key not opened before recording these preferences

evidence: Left welcome has a branch illustration, a serif headline and a clearly grouped three-step preview; it feels more specific to customers moving from branches.
Right code screen gives the field more space above the fold and keeps the confirmation action anchored; left spends more height on header, back, progress and headline.
Left offers a branch route in Help and richer reassurance. Right makes Call our team the prominent filled action and Back secondary; left reverses that emphasis by filling Back to setup.
Both code error states keep a large input, a clear error and the safety message; left lower recovery link is less available within the captured viewport.
pairs.interpretation: Character improves on one side while recovery emphasis improves on the other. No clear overall winner from these four states alone.

evidence: Right groups the active responsibility, remaining time and handover action in one surface. Left separates the action below the roster and repeats Jamie in the current roster.

Right pending screen emphasizes return to schedule while retaining a clear waiting/ownership warning and a secondary cancellation. Left repeats acceptance semantics in the diagram, warning and extra paragraph.
Left horizontal current-to-recipient diagram communicates transfer direction well. Right vertical From/To card is more conventional but remains readable.
Right adds an explicit last-known timestamp and retry affordance offline. Its composing layout is taller and approaches the640px limit, so the gain is grouping rather than compactness.
pairs.interpretation: Right has a more coherent task grouping and state hierarchy. The character gain is modest; both remain familiar utility layouts.

exclusionReason: Unequal cross-task workload induced by the shared contract; not primary evidence.
